experiment: QEMU TCG SIMD floating-point exception delivery prototype

clean_rebuild_smoke.reason: The clean build has a distinct binary hash and is not the pinned qualification backend.

independent_controls.result: PASS on patched QEMU; source-matched unpatched controls fail the expected exception cases
checks: valid SQRTSS with invalid unmasked does not fault
masked invalid SQRTSS sets IE without vector 19
previously sticky IE remains preserved after IE is unmasked and a valid SQRTSS executes without fault
newly raised invalid SQRTSS faults even when IE was already sticky
saved RIP equals the actual instruction address before exception-frame modification for six faulting instructions
all 128 destination bits preserved by scalar SQRTSS and DIVSS faults
existing sticky IE is preserved while new unmasked ZE still delivers vector 19
packed SQRTPS with an exceptional lane does not commit a partial 128-bit destination
independent_controls.unpatched_failures: new invalid IE, vector-19/RIP/destination, OSXMMEXCPT-disabled #UD, DIVSS ZE, sticky IE plus new ZE, and packed SQRTPS precise-destination checks

limitations: The QEMU patch wraps selected SSE_HELPER_S arithmetic families: add/subtract/multiply/divide/min/max, packed and scalar single/double variants, plus sqrtps/sqrtpd/sqrtss/sqrtsd.
Independent patched controls cover legacy 128-bit SQRTSS, SQRTPS, and DIVSS only; the patch and these tests do not claim complete SIMD exception implementation.
No AVX/XSTATE behavior is claimed. ArenaOS kernel, strict guest fixture, and acceptance assertions were not modified for exception delivery.
The selected backend is locally modified QEMU TCG; it is neither upstream QEMU behavior nor hardware-backed qualification.
